text:
Evan L: Hey folks, I'm going through benefits setup. My Gusto health coverage shows an effective date of 2027-03-01 but my offer says my first day was 2027-02-23 — which date actually applies for benefits? Also I have a transit pass receipt to submit, do we use Ramp or Expensify for one-off commuter reimbursements? Sorry if this is in the docs.

Asha (People Ops): Welcome aboard Evan! :tada: For most hires the benefits effective date follows the plan waiting period and will show in Gusto — so 2027-03-01 looks right for your hire. I can double-check your specific onboarding package if you want. For commuter reimbursements we generally use Ramp for employee one-offs; Expensify is reserved for vendor/contractor invoices. DM me the offer PDF and I'll confirm the effective date.

Miguel (Eng): FYI Evan — if you enrolled in commuter pre-tax you need to submit a statement each month too. Ramp has a quick flow for that.

Evan L: Thanks Asha, DM sent. Quick follow-up: holiday/PTO accrual — I started mid-week, does Redwood prorate my holiday and PTO for the first year? The handbook mentions prorating but not the formula.

Asha (People Ops): Yes, we prorate. Formula we use is roughly (days remaining in calendar year / 365) * annual allotment, rounded to the nearest half day. Example calc below:
```
Start: 2027-02-23
Days remaining: 310
Annual PTO: 18 days
Pro-rated: 18 * 310 / 365 = 15.3 -> 15.5 days
```
I'll add the exact number into your profile once I confirm with Payroll.

Payroll Bot: Heads up — first payroll run that will include your pay is 2027-03-05. If direct deposit isn't set by 2027-03-01 contact payroll@redwood.com.

Priya (Finance): For commuter reimbursements processed through Ramp, please tag receipts with the project code if the expense is >$150. Keep originals for audit (scan ok). If you need a one-off advance, ping me and we can route it.

Evan L: Awesome, super helpful — thanks everyone! I'll upload the transit receipt to Ramp now and confirm my bank details in Gusto. :thumbsup:
